main_text.p: nubes pluviam: quædam consequuntur; ut pallor morbum, vastatio regionis bellum: quædam conjuncta sunt cum reiut[?] inæqualis pulsatio arteriæ cum febri, tranquilitas conscientiæ cum justificatione. Atque ex his quædam dicuntur τεκμήρια[?], quædam εἰκότα[?]. Τεκμήρια dicuntur, quæ omni & soli rei signatæ conveniunt, atque adeò cum illa reciprocantur; ut aurora cum Solis ortu, fulmen cum tonitru: εἰκότα[?] dicuntur, quæ cum re signata non reciprocantur, eaque vel omni conveniunt, non soli; sic pallor est signum morbi; hæc vocantur signa æquivoca: quædam conveniunt soli, non omni; sic eclipsis est signum plenilunii: quædam nec omni, nec soli; veluti cum cutis hispida, dicitur signum falacitatis.
XIV. Circumstantia est id quod circa rem est, sive adiacet aut appositum est; huc pertinet locus, tempus, vestitus, armatura, & id genus alia.
main_text.head: CAP. XXIX.

head.i: De eo quod est Necessarium, Impos-sibile, Contingens & Possibile.

main_text.p: Necessarium generatim dicitur, quod non potest non esse: Necessario contrarium

page.notes: The Greek words τεκμήρια and εἰκότα are read from a small scan and marked [?]; their accents are uncertain. "reiut" (about "cum re ut") is uncertain, probably a printing error or a dropped letter. The second line of Thesis I continues on the next page with "trarium" (the word is "contrarium", split as "con-" / "trarium"); the printed hyphen is kept as "con-" only where it stands. The drop cap N in "Necessarium" is joined to the word. Lines of the thesis on the printed page: "Necessario con-" and "trarium" (the continuation "trarium" is at the right of the line below). No catchword, signature or notes in the margins.
